core_claims.claim: The National Polygon Dataset publishes HM Land Registry Index Polygons for England and Wales.
The National Polygon Dataset is closely linked to Title Descriptor and UPRN datasets.
The Title Descriptor dataset is linked to National Polygon and UPRN datasets.
A title number is a unique identifier that can link to other HM Land Registry data.
The UPRN lookup dataset contains HM Land Registry title numbers and Ordnance Survey AddressBase UPRNs.
The UPRN lookup dataset is linked to National Polygon and Title Descriptor datasets.
The three National Polygon Service datasets form a linked service family.
National Polygon Service data covers freehold and leasehold registered land and property.
A UPRN is retained for the lifetime of an addressable location.
The National Polygon dataset is a subset of the HM Land Registry Index Map.
National Polygon, Title Descriptor and UPRN lookup together comprise the National Polygon Service.
HM Land Registry public-data guidance lists the National Polygon Service among available data products.
A title number is HM Land Registry's reference for an individual piece of registered land.
The licensed National Polygon Service datasets are delivered through the Use land and property data service.
Dataset linkage depends on title-number identity rather than polygon proximity alone.
UPRN linkage does not guarantee that every title has exactly one addressable UPRN.
Polygon data represents registration indexing, not a surveyed legal boundary guarantee.
The service distinguishes polygon geometry from descriptive title attributes.
The service distinguishes title-number/UPRN lookup records from polygon features.
Exact GML bytes and hashes require direct file readback rather than technical-specification review.
Technical specifications establish field and relationship contracts but not the three target feature identities.
A title number can link across HMLR products only when the exact value is present in each relevant dataset.
UPRN lifecycle persistence does not establish current ownership, tenure or boundary accuracy.
Public catalogue availability does not remove licensing and service-access conditions.
Current INSPIRE identifiers for the three candidates remain unproven without candidate-specific feature readback.
Polygon linkage cannot produce elevation measurements without an independent elevation source.
Title-number linkage is necessary but not sufficient for numeric height-difference promotion.
Fail-closed candidate binding is required while exact GML features and identifiers are absent.
